day_shape: 74 items: Strait of Hormuz remains contested with CENTCOM claiming 59 vessels redirected under blockade and Iran insisting closure holds, UK joins 33-country statement on Iranian executions (916 since January), IDF Beit Lahiya strike kills Hamas commander, Iraq sets 30 September coalition withdrawal deadline.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz standoff and shipping
threads.summary: CENTCOM said US forces have redirected 59 commercial vessels, disabled 3 and boarded 2 enforcing a blockade, while Defa Press claimed the Strait remains closed until Iran's conditions are met and traffic hit a three-month low. Ambrey reported participating in a tanker rescue off Oman, Iran International reported oil slicks reaching Qeshm mangroves, and a separate US strike on a container ship near an Iranian port was reported.

threads.label: Gaza strikes and Board of Peace plan
threads.summary: The IDF confirmed an airstrike in Beit Lahiya killing a Hamas cell commander it said was planning attacks on troops, and disputed Avigdor Liberman's claim that it ignored a Hamas exercise. Jerusalem Post reported Liberman's claims that the 15-point Gaza Board of Peace plan grants Hamas's military wing $160 million and up to $400 million in debt relief, alongside reports of intensified Hamas interrogations of Gaza residents.

threads.label: Lebanon southern front and disarmament
threads.summary: Israeli Defense Minister Katz said the IDF "will not withdraw" from security zones, prompting Washington to state a permanent military presence in southern Lebanon is inconsistent with commitments, as IDF strikes hit Mansouri in Tyre. Britain, Italy, Switzerland and Indonesia were named as potential contributors to a mechanism to verify Hezbollah's disarmament, and Lebanon's parliament voted 128 to abolish the death penalty with Hezbollah's bloc opposing.

threads.label: Iran command reshuffle and hardliner shift
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post reported Iran's newly appointed military and IRGC leaders include sanctioned officials and figures linked to the 1994 AMIA bombing, filling vacancies from Israeli and US strikes. Iran International reported hardliners frame Mohsen Rezaei's appointment as security chief as a shift against negotiations, while an IRGC adviser said Tehran could prolong the war until Trump leaves office.

threads.label: UK-led statement on Iranian executions
threads.summary: The FCDO issued a joint statement with 33 countries and the EU High Representative on executions in Iran, while Iran International cited the Abdorrahman Boroumand Center reporting at least 916 executions in Iran since January including 15 in August. Canada separately said IRGC conscription alone is not a bar as Iranians who completed mandatory service face inadmissibility scrutiny.

threads.label: Regional theatres: Iraq, Yemen, Somalia
threads.summary: Iraq's ministerial council of national security set 30 September as the final deadline for the international coalition's mission to end, as Jerusalem Post reported PM Al-Zaidi's push to disarm Iran-backed militias. Ansarallah's Muhammad al-Bukhayti said Yemeni forces would target any Israeli presence in Somalia, and IRIB cited Pentagon figures of 153 Yemeni civilians killed in 2025 US strikes.

threads.label: Iran domestic pressure and diplomacy
threads.summary: Iran International reported over 152,000 severely disabled Iranians await nursing allowances, an Instagram poll suggesting eight in ten would leave Iran, and Iran's oil output remaining around a quarter below pre-war levels. Foreign Minister Araghchi attacked France over human rights preaching, and a senior Iranian source told Reuters there was nothing to extend of the US ceasefire as Tehran considered it never started.

events.title_en: Political alignment of Zionist parties on the eve of parliamentary elections
events.summary_en: Political alignment of Zionist parties on the eve of parliamentary elections. The Zionist regime is moving towards parliamentary elections in November whilst its political structure is embroiled in fragmentation and instability more than ever. The Knesset electoral system, which is built on the basis of unstable coalitions, now faces crises resulting from the Gaza war, internal pressures, and strategic failures against the axis of resistance. This situation has not only challenged the political fate of Benjamin Netanyahu and his secular rivals, but has also shrouded the future security of Gaza and this regime's regional policies in a haze of uncertainty.

events.title_en: Xavi became manager of the Dutch national football team
events.summary_en: Xavi became manager of the Dutch national football team. Xavi Hernández, former Barcelona coach and player, has taken over the management of the Dutch national football team with a four-year contract until 2030 and has replaced Ronald Koeman. Xavi began his managerial career in 2019 at Qatar's Al Sadd club, returned to Barcelona in 2021 and took over the management of that team as Koeman's successor. In the 2022-23 season, he managed to lead Barcelona to the Spanish league championship, but in 2024 he gave way to Hansi Flick.

events.title_en: Imam Reza (peace be upon him); intelligent politics at the heart of power
events.summary_en: Imam Reza (peace be upon him); intelligent politics at the heart of power. One of the essential axes in the thought of our martyred leader regarding the Imams is to view their lives as a single, continuous historical movement. In this framework, the difference in the conduct of the Imams does not mean a difference in purpose; rather it is the result of differences in the political and social conditions of each period. events.title_en: Imam Reza (peace be upon him); from imamate in an age of turmoil to martyrdom in exile
events.summary_en: Imam Reza (peace be upon him); from imamate in an age of turmoil to martyrdom in exile. His Eminence Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, peace be upon him, is the son of Imam al-Kadhim and the Eighth Imam of the Twelver Shi'a. His imamate lasted 20 years, which coincided with the caliphate of Harun al-Rashid, al-Amin, and al-Ma'mun of the Abbasids. That Imam, at the insistence and coercion of al-Ma'mun, travelled from Medina to the city of Merv in Khorasan, the seat of the caliphate of this Abbasid caliph. Al-Ma'mun forced Imam Reza to accept the title of heir-apparent, and eventually in 203 AH poisoned him and brought about his martyrdom. The place where his pure body was buried later became known as 'Mashhad al-Rida', which is today a major pilgrimage site for Shi'a worldwide.

events.title_en: Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz reaches lowest level in past three months
events.summary_en: Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz reaches lowest level in past three months. Analysis of statistics published by vessel traffic tracking organisations shows that the five-day average of ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz has reached its lowest point in the past three months. Examining data from the maritime tracking company Kepler shows that in the past five days, on average, only 13 vessels have passed through this international waterway. This figure is the lowest rate since 12 May to date. These statistics include all types of vessels, from cargo ships to oil tankers. This traffic is approximately 90 per cent lower than the daily average of maritime traffic before the war against Iran began.
